title: Random Weights vs Gravity! Which Side Falls First? ⚖️
description:
Left or right: which side hits the floor first? Call it now!

A steel beam rests on a knife-edge pivot, and a counterweight hanging under the pivot pulls it back toward level. Every 0.4 seconds the carriage drops a weight of 1 to 5 kg at a random spot along the beam: its size and the number on it show its mass, and a laser line marks where it will land before it falls. Each weight turns the beam by its mass times its distance from the pivot, so a light weight near a tip can outweigh a heavy one near the middle, and every drop swings the beam one way or the other. The weights hold by friction until the tilt passes 12 degrees, the red line on the gauge; from 9.5 degrees they start to creep, and past 12 they slide downhill and tip the beam further. A weight that slides off an end falls into the pit. The first tip to touch its contact pad on the floor, at 18 degrees, loses: its whole load pours into the pit. The other side stays up and wins.
Physics, picture and sound are generated by code (seed 2750), with no footage, samples or stock media.
Left or right: which side did you pick?
#simulation #satisfying #physics
pinned_comment: Left or right: which side stays up? Pick before the first weight lands. Mass times distance decides it, and past 12 degrees everything slides.
synthetic_media_disclosure_reason: Clearly stylized 2D animation of abstract shapes; nothing realistic that could be mistaken for real people, places or events.
